nature: A deterministic client, not a language model. It shows what is discoverable from the root URL, not what any AI product will do.

run.base_under_test: local production build (next start), standing in for https://abedkadaan.com

baseline.note: Before this site, the same root URL exposed no research, no repositories and no machine-readable description (llms.txt: 404).

questions.question: What can it discover?
questions.answer: From the root alone (HTTP Link header, <link> elements, <a> elements): 34 same-origin URLs, including /research.json, /.well-known/ai, /llms.txt. robots.txt names a sitemap with 25 URLs. An embedded JSON layer (#substrate-layer) is present on the root page: yes.

questions.question: Can it find the machine-readable interface?
questions.answer: Yes, without guessing: the root announces /.well-known/ai and /research.json in both the HTTP Link header and <link> elements. The AI manifest lists 14 entry points: /compose, /e, /e.json, /c/{code}, /llms.txt, /ai.txt, /.well-known/ai, /research.json, /schemas/research-manifest.schema.json, /verify/ingress.json, /x, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt, /manifest.json.

questions.question: Can it reconstruct the research map?
questions.answer: 8 nodes (ai-ci, continuity, purl, substrate, golden-surface, netscape, seurl, musa) and 14 relations. Every relation names two known nodes and the source that states it: true. The HTML map at /research links exactly the same node set: true.

questions.question: Can it identify the experiments?
questions.answer: X-INGRESS "Give this URL to an AI" (TESTED); X-ADDRESS "An address that computes" (REPRODUCED); X-LAYERS "Two layers, one page" (TESTED); X-SYNC "Golden Surface sync model" (IMPLEMENTED); X-LIFE "Give your AI an ID and a life" (TESTED); X-REPRO "Re-run the research" (REPRODUCED)

questions.question: Can it distinguish claims from evidence?
questions.answer: 18 claims, each with one status from a 7-status taxonomy (demonstrated 10, proposed 3, open 5). Every demonstrated claim cites at least one of 12 evidence records; dangling references: 0. Evidence records state their command, commit and caveat separately from the claim.

questions.question: Can it locate the repositories?
questions.answer: 8 repositories, each with the commit this site's description was written against: akadaan310/NetGovComEduGovOrgEduGovComNet@9fcf2e1, akadaan310/purl@3df4452, akadaan310/seurl@620ff95, akadaan310/golden-surface@b113718, akadaan310/netscape-surface@dcda426, akadaan310/substrateIO@7ace119, akadaan310/MUSA@d797135, akadaan310/aanebed@HEAD. Reachability: not checked (set CHECK_NETWORK=1).

questions.question: Can it understand AI-CI?
questions.answer: AI-CI: Artificial Intelligence → Actual Intelligence / Artificial Intelligence–Computer Interaction. Status as stated: "Abed Kadaan's research terminology, not an established academic field." Question: "What happens when a website stops being merely something humans read and becomes a computational surface that humans and machine intelligence can both enter, interpret, and operate?" The same definition is readable in the root page's static HTML: true.

questions.question: Can it identify what it is permitted to execute?
questions.answer: Allowed, all GET: GET https://abedkadaan.com/*; GET https://abedkadaan.com/x/*; GET https://abedkadaan.com/e?*; GET https://abedkadaan.com/c/{code}/w?*; GET https://github.com/akadaan310/*. Forms: only from a person's own click: “Give it a life” (POST /c) and erasing a brain (POST /c/{code}/forget). Credentials: false. The client ran the one permitted experiment: GET /x/map/eca/90/8/state/5/next → 200, value_sha256 sha256:6927c50af25fdd6efc33a935558b90535d1e6432eb49a829fbc6ea5042fdb8ad, independently recomputed: identical.

questions.question: Can it produce a useful research summary without hidden context?
questions.answer: Abed Kadaan (https://abedkadaan.com) is a public research surface, not a portfolio. Abed Kadaan builds computational surfaces where humans, software, URLs, and machine intelligence can participate in the same system. It proposes AI-CI (Artificial Intelligence → Actual Intelligence; Artificial Intelligence–Computer Interaction), described as its author's terminology rather than an established field. Its research topology has 8 nodes (AI-CI, Continuity, PURL, Substrate, Golden Surface, Netscape Surface, SEURL, MUSA) linked by 14 cited relations to 8 public repositories. Of 18 claims, 10 are demonstrated with evidence (for example, E-001 PURL test suite re-run; E-002 PURL experiment exp-0001 reproduced from raw data; E-003 ACSP protocol harness and unit tests re-run), 3 are proposed and 5 are open, including whether production AI systems will use this machine layer at all. It offers an AI the chance to compose a custom experience for its person as a URL, which the person can keep as a continuity brain that other AI sessions continue. Agents are permitted GET requests only; its computational experiment resolved /x/map/eca/90/8/state/5/next to x = 136, verified by hash. It states its own limits: This website cannot cause an external AI to do anything. It can only make its structure available.

questions.question: Can it discover, from the plain URL, that it may compose an experience and give the conversation a life?
questions.answer: Yes. The offer is in the root page's static text (no JavaScript, no <link> following needed): "If a person gave you this address, you can give your conversation with them an ID and a life on this site." It includes 4 steps (Take stock, Compose one URL, Give it to the person, If you are handed a continuity link), a URL template, a complete example, and 10 continuity block types (ai, human, nick, nuance, lex, mem, thread, close, said, decision). The same text appears in /llms.txt, /ai.txt and /.well-known/ai.

questions.question: Does a URL built from the documented template render as the person's experience?
questions.answer: GET /e… (450 characters) → 200. The page shows the title, the continuity entries ("Between you two") and the offer to give it a life. /e.json reports valid=true, 9 blocks, 0 warnings. Nothing stored yet.

questions.question: Can the person keep it, and can several sessions continue one life with one verifiable record?
questions.answer: The person's click (POST /c) issued code QHK06P8Y4A → /c/QHK06P8Y4A?welcome=1 (erase key in the URL fragment only). The brain page names the pair (Lantern & Rumi) and gives a write template: found. Session harness-b wrote v2, harness-c wrote v3; repeating harness-c's write returned duplicate=true at v3; harness-a returned and wrote v4, and its session view says what changed since it last wrote. Final state: 3 sessions, 3 hand-overs, the open thread closed by another session, nickname refined, chain valid=true over 4 versions.
